name: Govindānanda
text:
## In short

Govindānanda of Navadvīpa, «overwhelmed with ecstatic love»: by remembering him the ten directions are purified.

## In the book

- At the nightly kīrtanas in Śrīvāsa's house (Madhya 8.112–116) and on the night of the Kazi among the leaders of kīrtana (Madhya 23.150–152).
- Weeping when the Lord left Navadvīpa: «Govinda, Govindānanda, Śrīgarbha, Śrīmān, Kāśīśvara, Śrī Jagadānanda, and Rāma also began to cry» (Madhya 23.451).
- To Purī for the Ratha-yātrā: «Govindānanda, who was overwhelmed with ecstatic love of God, also came. By remembering him, the ten directions are purified» (Antya 8.16).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 8.112–116, 23.150–152, 23.451; Antya 8.16.

name: Hiraṇya Ṭhākura
text:
## In short

Hiraṇya Paṇḍita («Hiraṇya Bhāgavata») of Navadvīpa, a poor brāhmaṇa and friend of Jagannātha Miśra: the child Nimāi ate the Ekādaśī offering of his house, and later Nityānanda stayed with him, when the dacoits came for His ornaments.

## Ekādaśī: the child Nimāi eats their offering (Ādi 6.20–34)

The child Nimāi cried and would not stop: «If you want to save My life, then go quickly to the house of the two brāhmaṇas… Jagadīśa and Hiraṇya are both great devotees, and I desire something from them. Today is Ekādaśī, and they are both fasting. But they have prepared varieties of foodstuffs for Lord Viṣṇu. If I could eat their offering, I will be cured.» Śacī lamented — such a thing is not sanctioned in the Vedas or in custom. «Those two brāhmaṇas were great Vaiṣṇavas and dearest friends of Jagannātha Miśra.» Hearing the request they were delighted: «How did He know that today is Ekādaśī? How did He know that we have prepared all kinds of foodstuffs for the Lord?… Lord Nārāyaṇa performs pastimes through the body of this child.» They brought all the offerings: «Dear child, please eat these foodstuffs. Our desire to serve Kṛṣṇa is fulfilled today.»

The *bhāṣya* (6.21–23): the two brāhmaṇas Jagadīśa Paṇḍita and Hiraṇya Paṇḍita lived in **Godrumadvīpa**, some distance from the Lord's house; the fast of Ekādaśī is for the living entities, not for Viṣṇu, the enjoyer of all offerings — so the devotees cook for Him on His day. (6.27: «Hiraṇya and Jagadīśa were the heart and soul of Jagannātha Miśra.»)

The *bhāṣya* on Ādi 2.98–99 quotes the *Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā* (192): Jagadīśa and Hiraṇya were the wives of the *yājñika* brāhmaṇas of Vraja (who fed Kṛṣṇa); and (143) Jagadīśa Paṇḍita was the dancer Candrahāsa.

## Nityānanda in his house (Antya 5.535–536)

> hiraṇya paṇḍita nāme eka subrāhmaṇa
> sei navadvīpe vaise — mahā-akiñcana

«In Navadvīpa there lived one qualified brāhmaṇa named Hiraṇya Paṇḍita, who had no material assets. Nityānanda left His associates and quietly resided in the house of that fortunate Hiraṇya Paṇḍita.» (The *bhāṣya*: freedom from possessions is a symptom of a qualified brāhmaṇa.) A wicked brāhmaṇa then gathered dacoits to rob the Avadhūta of His gold and pearls in Hiraṇya's house; they found the devotees awake, chanting and roaring all night (5.537 ff.), and were in the end delivered by Nityānanda.

## Other mentions

Born in Navadvīpa before the Lord (Ādi 2.31); came to Purī: «Śrī Jagadīśa Paṇḍita and Hiraṇya Bhāgavata, who were both intoxicated in the mellows of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, also joyfully came» (Antya 8.28).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 1.100; 2.31, 2.98–99 (bhāṣya); 6.20–34; Antya 5.535–556, 8.28.

name: Nandana Ācārya
text:
## In short

Nandana Ācārya, a *mahā-bhāgavata* of Navadvīpa: Nityānanda first stayed in his house; Advaita hid there; and there the Lord Himself hid one night, and spent it talking of Kṛṣṇa with him.

## Nityānanda comes to Navadvīpa (Madhya 3.123–176)

Nityānanda «immediately went to Navadvīpa, where He stayed at the house of Nandana Ācārya. Nandana Ācārya was a *mahā-bhāgavata*. He saw that the bodily effulgence of Nityānanda was equal to the sun.» He welcomed Him, fed Him and kept Him in his house (3.135); then «Śrī Gaurasundara led all the devotees to the house of Nandana Ācārya» (3.176), where the Lord and Nityānanda met. The *bhāṣya* (3.124): Nityānanda's gravity and patience, those of the topmost *avadhūta*, were seen by Nandana Ācārya.

## Advaita hides there (Madhya 6.57–69)

To test the Lord, Advaita said to Rāmāi: «I will secretly stay in the house of Nandana Ācārya, but you tell Him, “He has not come.”» But the Lord said: «I know Nāḍā is hiding at the house of Nandana Ācārya and He has sent you to test Me.»

## The Lord hides in his house (Madhya 17.47–68)

After punishing Advaita, the Lord told Nityānanda and Haridāsa to tell no one, and went to Nandana Ācārya's house, where He sat on the throne of Lord Viṣṇu. Nandana fell flat to offer obeisances, brought Him new clothes for His wet ones, decorated Him with sandalwood, garlands and *prasāda*, and offered camphor and betel: «The Lord forgot all His distress by the service of the pious Nandana Ācārya.» — «O Nandana, listen to Me. Today you should hide Me here.» —

> «O Lord, this is very difficult. Where can You hide within this world? You could not hide in the hearts of the living entities. The devotees exposed You even from there. How can one who could not hide in the ocean of milk hide in an open society?» (17.60–62)

The Lord smiled and passed the night there; «the fortunate Nandana Ācārya spent the entire night discussing the unlimited topics of Kṛṣṇa with the Lord». At dawn the Lord sent him: «Go and bring Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita alone.»

## Later

Among the leaders of kīrtana on the night of the Kazi (Madhya 23.150–152); among those who wept at the Lord's departure; and to Purī: «Nandana Ācārya, in whose house Lord Nityānanda first stayed, also came along in ecstasy» (Antya 8.22).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 3.123–176, 6.57–69, 17.47–68, 23.150–152; Antya 8.22.

name: Sadāśiva Paṇḍit
text:
## In short

Sadāśiva Paṇḍita of Navadvīpa, «pure-hearted», one of the first to whom the Lord opened His heart after Gayā; Nityānanda had stayed in his house. With Buddhimanta Khān he got the costumes for the Lord's drama.

## In the book

- **Born before the Lord** in Navadvīpa (Ādi 2.31).
- **After Gayā** (Madhya 1.40, 1.70, 1.81, 1.108): «You and Sadāśiva should come early tomorrow to Śuklāmbara Brahmacārī's house» — «I wish to reveal My distress to you, Sadāśiva, and Murāri Paṇḍita.» He was among those gathered there, «filled with amazement».
- **The drama** (Madhya 18.7–16): «The Lord called Sadāśiva and Buddhimanta Khān and told them, “Arrange for some costumes.”» They went home in unlimited ecstasy and brought conch-shells, bodices, silk sāris and ornaments (chapter summary).
- **To Purī** (Antya 8.19):

> «The pure-hearted Sadāśiva Paṇḍita, in whose house Nityānanda previously resided, also came.»

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 2.31; Madhya 1.40–108, 18.7–16; Antya 8.19.

name: Śrīman Paṇḍit
text:
## In short

Śrīmān Paṇḍita of Navadvīpa brought the devotees the first news that Nimāi Paṇḍita, back from Gayā, had become «the greatest Vaiṣṇava»; in the kīrtanas and in the Lord's drama he held the torch.

## The news (Madhya 1.51–78)

He had visited the Lord the day before: «Śrīmān Paṇḍita was filled with joy. He was delighted to see the Lord's wonderful manifestation of love.» The next morning, at the inexhaustible *kunda* tree in Śrīvāsa's house where the devotees gathered flowers, he arrived smiling. — «It seems you are very happy today?» — «There is, of course, a good reason… A most wonderful and most impossible incident has occurred: Nimāi Paṇḍita has become the greatest Vaiṣṇava.» He told how the Lord, as soon as He mentioned Pāda-padma-tīrtha, filled the place with tears, trembled, cried «O Kṛṣṇa!» and fell unconscious: «By the devotion that I have seen in Him, I no longer consider Him an ordinary human being.» The Lord had said: «Let us meet at Śuklāmbara's house early tomorrow morning. I wish to reveal My distress to you, Sadāśiva, and Murāri Paṇḍita.» The devotees chanted «Hari!» and Śrīvāsa said: «May Kṛṣṇa increase our family.» Śrīmān then went to Śuklāmbara's house on the Gaṅgā, where they gathered (1.78–81).

The *bhāṣya* (1.60): the same Nimāi Paṇḍita who a few days before was the crest jewel of logicians and ridiculed the Vaiṣṇavas had now become a great Vaiṣṇava.

## The torch (Madhya 18.11, 18.157; Antya 8.21)

For His drama the Lord assigned: «Śrīvāsa will dress as Nārada… Śrīmān will volunteer to hold the torch» (18.11); «Śrīmān Paṇḍita held a lamp before the Lord, and Haridāsa alerted everyone in the four directions» (18.157). Going to Purī for the Ratha-yātrā: «Śrīmān Paṇḍita chanted, “Hari bol!” as he came. He carried a torch to light the way when the Lord performed kīrtana» (Antya 8.21).

The *bhāṣya* (Ādi 2.98–99): Śrīmān Paṇḍita, a resident of Navadvīpa and participant in the Lord's inauguration of kīrtana, held a torch when the Lord danced in the mood of the goddess (*Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 10.37: the fifteenth branch).

## Other mentions

Among the devotees born in Navadvīpa before the Lord (Ādi 2.98–99); weeping when the Lord left for sannyāsa (Madhya 23.451).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 2.98–99; Madhya 1.51–81, 18.11, 18.157, 23.451; Antya 8.21.

name: Īśāna Ṭhākura
text:
## In short

Īśāna, the domestic servant of the Lord's house, who served Śacī-mātā all his life: «the most fortunate person within the fourteen worlds».

## The lunch of Gaura and Nitāi (Madhya 8.58–74)

When the Lord brought Nityānanda home for lunch, «Īśāna gave them water to wash their feet». Serving Them, Śacī saw Them as two five-year-old boys with four arms, one whitish, one blackish, and her daughter-in-law on the chest of her son; she fell unconscious and rice was scattered all over the room. Afterwards:

> īśāna karila saba gṛha upaskāra
> yata chila avaśeṣa — sakala tāṅhāra
> sevilena sarva-kāla āire īśāna
> caturdaśa loka madhye mahā-bhāgyavān

«Then Īśāna cleaned the entire room and honored all the remnants. Īśāna is the most fortunate person within the fourteen worlds, for he served Mother Śacī throughout his entire life.» (8.73–74)

The *bhāṣya*: Īśāna, the Lord's domestic servant, gathered the scattered rice and cleaned the room; there is no limit to his good fortune — he served the Lord's mother and wife even after the Lord took sannyāsa.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 8.58–74.

name: Jagadīśa Paṇḍita (of Navadvīpa)
text:
## In short

Jagadīśa Paṇḍita of Navadvīpa (Godrumadvīpa), friend of Jagannātha Miśra: with Hiraṇya he gave the child Nimāi the Ekādaśī offering prepared for Viṣṇu.

Born in Navadvīpa before the Lord (Ādi 2.31, 2.98–99); in the kīrtanas (Madhya 8.112–116, 23.150–152); came to Purī: «Śrī Jagadīśa Paṇḍita and Hiraṇya Bhāgavata, who were both intoxicated in the mellows of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, also joyfully came» (Antya 8.28).

(The *bhāṣya* on Ādi 2.98–99 also quotes Antya 5.736 — «Jagadīśa Paṇḍita was the abode of great effulgence. Nityānanda and His associates were his life and soul» — for this Jagadīśa; see also #534.)

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 1.100; 2.31, 2.98–99; 6.20–34; Madhya 8.112–116, 23.150–152; Antya 8.28.
